title: Hybrid streaming aggregator for per-route/model/customer cost & latency breakdowns
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Console currently shows coarse-grained cost and latency numbers that are computed offline and diverge from near-real-time usage and billing windows. Teams need per-route, per-model, and per-customer breakdowns that align with billing, support fast investigation of regressions (p50/p95/p99 latency changes), and enable cost-optimization recommendations in Redwood Optimize.

Goals: Provide a single, authoritative service that computes: total token counts (prompt vs. generated), inference latency percentiles, and dollar cost breakdowns (GPU/CPU amortized + infra overhead) by route, model, and customer. The service must support both near-real-time views (1m, 5m rollups) for the Console and high-fidelity daily rollups that feed billing and chargeback.

Constraints & non‑goals: Not responsible for final invoicing (billing pipeline owns monetary reconciliation). Must avoid double-charging when requests hit fallbacks or multi-model routing. We will not re-architect serving traces; we rely on existing runtime request logs, KV-cache hit signals, and the token accounting ledger produced by ENG-20489.

High-level approach: Build a hybrid streaming-windowed aggregator implemented with Apache Flink for stateful sessionization and near-real-time rollups, with periodic micro-batch materialization to ClickHouse for low-latency Console queries. Key ideas:
- Ingest streams: request_trace (per-request timing + route/model/customer + tokens_decoded/encoded), runtime_metrics (GPU/host utilization and instance-level cost rates), and model_profiles (cost-per-token/time-per-token side input updated hourly).
- Sessionize by request_id and output an enriched event that includes: model_variant, route_id, customer_id, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, decode_seconds, kv_cache_hit (boolean), fallback_chain (list).
- Windowing strategy: rolling 1m windows for near-real-time, tumbling hourly for operational dashboards, daily for billing alignment. Use incremental combiners to keep memory bounded.
- Cost allocation: compute raw inference_seconds = sum(decode_seconds) per window; gpu_cost = inference_seconds * instance_gpu_hourly_rate/3600; infra_overhead = percent overhead by customer_tier; then attribute cost to tokens with an adjustable formula: cost_per_token = (gpu_cost + infra_overhead) / billable_tokens_with_kv_adjustment. KV cache hits reduce billable tokens by configured multiplier (e.g., 0.2 for served from KV).
- Latency metrics: compute request-level client_latency_ms and server_decode_ms; report p50/p95/p99 and count. Provide histogram export compatible with Console histograms.

Deliverables:
- Flink job repo and CI (github PR: link below).
- ClickHouse materialized tables: route_cost_rollup, model_cost_rollup, customer_cost_rollup with schema documented in design doc.
- Console read API endpoints (internal) to surface 1m/1h/1d rollups.
- Evaluation dashboard showing reconciliation with billing ledger and example alerts for regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Near-real-time (<=60s) 1m rollups available in ClickHouse for 90% of requests.
2) Daily aggregates reconcile to billing ledger within 0.5% on high-volume customers (subject to billing pipeline adjustments).
3) Console can fetch and display p50/p95/p99 latency and total cost per-route for a selected day range.

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- Chose Flink over micro-batch Spark for lower tail latency and stateful sessionization. Trade-off: higher operational complexity and need for backing state storage.
- ClickHouse chosen for read performance in Console; we will export the same rollups to BigQuery for archival/billing reconciliation.
- To avoid double counting during model fallbacks, the enrichment step tags events with fallback_chain and we attribute cost only to the final served_model with a traceable mapping.
- Sampling: low-volume customers (thresholded by tokens/day) will be sampled for 1m rollups and fully processed in hourly/daily windows to save CPU. Sampling policy is configurable and recorded in metadata.

Operational runbook (short):
- If Flink job lag > 2m: check Kafka backlog, restart job with savepoint restore if necessary.
- If reconciliation drift >1% for 3 consecutive days: open incident and run detailed diff between route_cost_rollup and billing ledger slices.

Schema highlights (human-readable):
- route_cost_rollup: window_start, window_end, route_id, model_id, customer_id, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, total_decode_seconds, gpu_cost_usd, infra_overhead_usd, total_cost_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, request_count

Longer-term ideas (future): multi-tenant cost rate models per region, per-instance-type breakdowns, and automatic anomaly detection to push recommendations into Redwood Optimize.

notes: This ticket is intended to replace the ad-hoc windowing logic currently in the analytics cluster and become the single source of truth for Console cost/latency surface. Coordinate with platform SRE on Flink cluster sizing and state-backend retention.
